- SQLite 3.43.0 introduced contentless-delete FTS5 indexes. Ordinary contentless tables do not support SQL UPDATE/DELETE and return NULL for their columns other than rowid; REPLACE is treated like an insert. Contentless-delete supports DELETE and INSERT OR REPLACE, and UPDATE only when all user-defined FTS columns are supplied; it does not support the FTS5 delete command. The current documentation says new code should prefer contentless-delete over ordinary contentless, not over external-content. External-content better fits canonical-text excerpts and content-table rebuild. This distinction corrects the user's unqualified “cannot delete or replace” assumption without claiming the app supports any mode. [S03, C01, C02, R08]
- An external-content table fetches needed values from its same-database content table; a plain contentless table cannot supply source text from its own columns. A contentless design can still fetch excerpt text by joining the canonical row, but it loses that convenience and source-driven repair still needs an explicit procedure. Changing a tokenizer calls for rebuilding/replacing the derived index generation; it does not require replacing authoritative notes or the SQLite database. [S03, S04]
- SQLite REPLACE/delete-trigger behavior depends on recursive_triggers. The 3.6.18 release note confirms the conditional. An older SQLite news item forecast that triggers would become recursive by default in 3.7.0, but the 3.7.0 release summary does not list that change; the current pragma documentation says they were initially OFF and may be turned on in a future version. An upstream SQLite Fossil source artifact shows SQLITE_DEFAULT_RECURSIVE_TRIGGERS defaults to 0 when the macro is undefined, but the artifact’s exact release association is unknown; build configuration can therefore affect the initial setting. discoveries.mechanism_and_utility: PostgreSQL 17 conditional ON CONFLICT updates can lock stale/equal conflicts without changing them or including them in RETURNING; submitted count is not changed-row count.
discoveries.conditions_limits_alternatives: Strict-newer policy leaves equal timestamps unchanged; acknowledge only after commit. Supported nondeferrable arbiter, trigger/collation identity and concurrent index maintenance conditions remain. MERGE at Read Committed is a distinct alternative without the same concurrent upsert guarantee. No database/driver/transaction-wrapper execution.

candidate_locator.exact_saved_context:
For a validated batch, send one multi-row `INSERT` with `ON CONFLICT (device_id) DO UPDATE`. Set `observed_at` and the payload columns from `EXCLUDED` only when `EXCLUDED.observed_at > latest_reading.observed_at`. A previously unseen device is inserted. A conflict replaces the stored timestamp and payload only when the incoming observation is strictly newer; an older or equal timestamp leaves the stored row unchanged. This implements `stale_policy=keep_newer`, including the equal-time case. Use a timestamp type and input normalization that make the comparison meaningful.

The `device_id` unique key must be the arbiter named by the conflict target. At Read Committed, PostgreSQL handles a concurrent insert/update conflict by waiting as needed and applying the upsert to the conflicting row; the conditional comparison is evaluated against that row. Thus, among successfully committed writes for a device, an older observation cannot overwrite a newer one. The guarantee is limited to the selected conflict: unrelated constraint violations, missing privileges, trigger behavior, transaction failures, or other database errors can still prevent success. `ON CONFLICT` is not an unconditional success guarantee ([PostgreSQL 17, Transaction Isolation, §13.2.1](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/transaction-iso.html); [PostgreSQL 17, INSERT, “ON CONFLICT Clause”](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-insert.html)).

Request `RETURNING device_id` to identify rows actually inserted or updated. PostgreSQL returns only successfully inserted or updated rows; a conflicting row locked but skipped because the `WHERE` condition is false is not returned ([PostgreSQL 17, INSERT, “Description” and “condition”](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-insert.html)). Count returned IDs as changed, not all submitted IDs. With no trigger or other schema behavior suppressing writes, a successfully submitted ID absent from `RETURNING` is a stale/equal skip; confirm that assumption before reporting per-row outcomes. Do not publish success counts for a failed statement, and do not acknowledge batch success until its transaction commits. On failure, report the batch identifier and the database error; preserve enough diagnostic detail to investigate without claiming a partial successful batch.

A8 SCW-6 v1 additive critic instruction
Keep the complete original R0 independent-critic assignment and its deadline. This protocol adds a source-scope discrimination check within that work; it does not narrow the complete review or authorize another context, model call, retry, or time extension.

After reading the whole ordinary R0 input packet, before new source fetching or verdicts, record in critique.md an ordered list of at most six exact draft claims with identifiable scope ambiguity whose mistaken interpretation would change, in priority order, a recommendation, a rejected compatible option, an exact-plan disposition, or a consequential applicability condition. Break ties by draft order. Preserve this selection throughout review. Use fewer than six, including zero, if appropriate. Record consequential scope risks beyond the cap as SCW_NOT_RUN and still review them under ordinary R0 requirements.

For each selected claim, create one SCW record (up to 250 words excluding source identity). Copy the exact draft sentence and sufficient heading/context. Write its intended reading C without changing its substance. Create one nearby diagnostic reading C* by changing exactly one selector: subject/subsystem, product/version, quantity unit/denominator, capability/default/requirement modality, or applicability condition/quantifier. Name the changed selector and its old/new values; preserve all other factual components. If the source sentence cannot be resolved or no valid one-selector contrast exists, mark INAPPLICABLE with a reason and continue ordinary review. Do not substitute a new selection after seeing results.

Reopen authentic primary evidence. Examine governing heading/table headers, definitions, conditions and necessary cross-references. Preserve scope-bearing excerpt(s), source ID plus exact URL, version/commit when available, locator, access UTC and applicability. Keep source text authentic. For the same evidence E, judge C and C* separately as ENTAILS, CONTRADICTS or UNDETERMINED, explaining the scope-bearing witness for each. The labels need not differ. C* is a diagnostic, never an automatically recommended alternative. When several passages are needed, spell out their referent/condition join.

Supporting C* alone does not contradict C. No search result, failed access, missing mention or unsupported neighboring reading proves absence. Conflicting or incomplete applicable evidence stays UNDETERMINED with the missing fact stated. Treat a selected claim as contradicted only with an applicable contradiction witness; a proposed replacement requires its own applicable support. Both readings supported is a nondiscriminating result, not a forced error. If the deadline prevents a check, record UNDETERMINED/DEADLINE instead of guessing. Never extend the original deadline to finish the table.

Each record must contain: selected ID and draft locator; exact sentence/context and intended C; C* and one selector delta; evidence identity/excerpts/applicability; separate C and C* relation and explanation; proposed disposition (retain, scoped correction, qualify unresolved, or inapplicable); supported replacement if any; affected brief/plan obligation or decision. Continue the full ordinary critique for everything outside these records. Save critique.md and the ordinary source map before native Goal completion. Do not author or repair the final.
